finding: A query cancellation completed after the final pre-lock checkpoint but before queue insertion could still allow a successful send. A separate actual quota error could be masked by payload destruction triggering cancellation.
design: The session exposes a fixed single-item VecDeque publication operation rather than a lifecycle lock guard or callback. It reserves a slot before the lifecycle lock and moves the item only while the same lifecycle lock as query cancellation is held. Failed publication returns ownership; queue code rolls back tracker state and disables acknowledgement, releases tracker and queue locks, records first failure, then drops the item.

red.observation: Cancellation completed before insertion but send returned Ok.

fault_red.observation: QuotaExceeded was masked by cancellation from a generic payload destructor.

prior_prototype: Early green/final/owned_regression/wait_regression records describe an abandoned public lock-guard prototype, not the final implementation; the public guard was removed. Subsequent fixed1, reentrant, session and combined records precede later source/test changes and are retained as history.
limitations: Tests use controlled in-process interleavings and one injected mutex poison. The session ordering test uses a bounded wait and does not establish exhaustive scheduling. Query/session locks serialize the observed publication and cancellation, but no production IPC, all lifecycle paths, RSS, platform or performance qualification follows. The deadline check is an instantaneous admission check, not a guarantee that a wall-clock deadline cannot pass immediately before insertion. The queue entry allocation and input byte work are not proven as RSS limits.
